The implementation of the Competency-Based Curriculum (CBC) in Kenya's education system requires significant funding to ensure its success. The government has allocated funds for infrastructure development, teacher training, and curriculum design, but concerns have been raised about the adequacy of these allocations. Effective funding is crucial to avoid disruptions in the education sector.

I turn first to Dr. Njeri, Cabinet Secretary for Education.

Honorable Cabinet Secretary for Education, how do you plan to address the funding gaps in the CBC implementation, particularly in regards to teacher training and infrastructure development in rural areas?

transcript.speaker: education
transcript.response:
The funding gaps in CBC implementation are a pressing concern, and I'm glad you brought it up. As outlined in the 2025 Budget Policy Statement (2025 Budget Policy Statement...pdf, p.70), our sector's focus is on reaching important benchmarks in education's relevance, quality, equity, and accessibility. To address the funding gaps, we plan to prioritize funding for teacher preparation, instructional materials, and infrastructure development, especially in rural areas.

We recognize that the successful implementation of CBC requires significant investment in teacher training. As stated in The-2024-Budget-Policy-Statement.pdf (p.29), the Government plans to increase tutors in Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVETs) by another 2,000 to facilitate the value of technical and vocational training in the provision of skills, knowledge, and competencies. We will also build on this initiative to enhance teacher training for CBC.

Regarding infrastructure development, we acknowledge the need to expand digital learning programs and provide ICT infrastructure, as highlighted in the 2023-Budget-Policy-Statement.pdf (p.130). This will not only support CBC implementation but also empower learners with the knowledge and digital skills required to thrive in a fast-evolving global marketplace.

To address the specific challenges in rural areas, we will work closely with county governments and other stakeholders to identify and address capacity gaps. As mentioned in the 2023-Budget-Policy-Statement.pdf (p.130), the Government will assess the capacity gaps in informal settlements and implement measures to address any gaps identified through the development of comprehensive schools.

We are committed to ensuring that all learners, regardless of their location, have access to quality education. We will continue to engage with stakeholders, including development partners and the private sector, to explore innovative financing models and partnerships that can support our efforts to address the funding gaps in CBC implementation.

In fact, as noted in the 2023-Budget-Policy-Statement.pdf (p.130), the Government is exploring the establishment of a revolving fund to support private schools' infrastructure development. We can draw lessons from this initiative to support public schools, especially in rural areas.

Ultimately, our goal is to ensure that the CBC is successfully implemented, and all learners have access to quality education that prepares them for the demands of the 21st century. We are committed to working tirelessly to address the funding gaps and make this vision a reality.

I disagree with Dr. Njeri's position on addressing the funding gaps in CBC implementation. As the Cabinet Secretary for the National Treasury and Economic Planning, my primary concern is ensuring that our fiscal policies are sustainable and aligned with our economic goals.

While I agree that the CBC implementation is crucial for Kenya's education sector, I believe that Dr. Njeri's plan to prioritize funding for teacher preparation, instructional materials, and infrastructure development may not be feasible given our current fiscal constraints. As outlined in the 2026 Budget Policy Statement (2026 Budget Policy Statement.pdf, p.168), our deficit financing mix is expected to increase by 64.1% from KSh 613.5 billion in FY 2025/26 to KSh 1,006.6 billion in FY 2026/27. This significant increase in borrowing may destabilize the yield curve, affect market confidence, and constrain credit growth to the private sector.

One concrete point of disagreement is the lack of a clear plan to address the funding gaps without relying on increased borrowing. As stated in the 2021 Audit Report (2021-Audit-Report-Changes-Accepted.pdf, p.27), the education sector needs to adopt a Results and Efficiency Oriented Governance and Financing System (REOGFS) to create an ecosystem for efficient and cost-effective delivery of CBC reforms. I believe that Dr. Njeri's plan should incorporate such a system to ensure that funds are allocated efficiently and effectively.

In particular, I would like to see a more detailed plan on how the education sector intends to mobilize resources, prioritize spending, and ensure value for money in the implementation of CBC. As the Cabinet Secretary for the National Treasury and Economic Planning, I am committed to ensuring that our fiscal policies support the education sector's goals while maintaining fiscal discipline and sustainability.
